Former Bank of England Deputy Governor Jon Cunliffe Joins Fnality as UK Chair

Former Bank of England Deputy Governor Jon Cunliffe has joined blockchain wholesale settlement firm Fnality as chairman of its UK operating entity, according to Bloomberg.

Former Bundesbank payments chief Jochen Metzger has also joined Fnality Europe’s supervisory board and is expected to become its chair. Backed by institutions including Goldman Sachs, UBS, Santander, Bank of America and Citi, Fnality is seeking regulatory approval to launch dollar and euro versions of its institutional wholesale payment system. —

Nasdaq Invests $100M in Kraken Parent Payward at $21 Billion Valuation

According to Bloomberg, Nasdaq is investing $100 million in Payward, the parent company of cryptocurrency exchange Kraken, through its venture investment arm. The capital injection values Payward at $21 billion and deepens a strategic partnership established between the two firms in March, according to people familiar with the matter. The collaboration aims to accelerate the buildout of next-generation market infrastructure designed to support the trading, settlement, and custody of tokenized equities. — link

U.S. Treasury Triples Long-Bond Buyback to $6 Billion as Yields Hit Multi-Year Highs

The U.S. Treasury will buy back up to $6 billion of 10- to 20-year Treasuries on Sept. 10, triple the size of its previous long-dated operation, as part of plans to expand buybacks and improve liquidity in the world’s largest sovereign bond market. The move follows a bond selloff that pushed 30-year yields to their highest since 2007; yields continued rising after the announcement, with the benchmark 10-year yield reaching 4.8528%, its highest since November 2023. — link
